title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
A deepfake pornography system operated on a platform with 13 million monthly visitors, using AI to superimpose the faces of Dutch public figures onto sexual footage. The deployment had no meaningful human check at the platform level. Users who uploaded material were encouraged to remain anonymous to avoid prosecution and could earn money when videos gained views. The system was therefore incentivized to proliferate without moderation.

The failure was not that the technology existed, but that it was deployed in a commercial environment designed to reward its use for making nonconsensual sexual imagery of real people. Detection would have required either platform moderators reviewing uploads or some automated system designed to identify and remove such content before it spread. Neither appears to have been in place.

It is not established whether the platform operators created the deepfake technology themselves, profited directly from uploads, or knew the full scope of what was being distributed on their site.

summary:
Several female Dutch celebrities are considering filing police reports after discovering manipulated pornographic videos featuring their faces on an online platform that attracts 13 million visitors monthly. The videos depict various Dutch public figures, including entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, ministers, mayors, and members of the royal family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and encouraged victims to report them to authorities. Managers and representatives of different victims confirmed to the news organization that complaints have been filed or legal action is being considered.

These deepfake videos are created by superimposing a celebrity's face onto pornographic footage. Users who upload the material receive advice to remain anonymous, likely to avoid prosecution, and earn more money when videos gain views. Lawyers warn that without government intervention, more fake pornographic videos featuring celebrities will appear. Deepfakes fall under revenge pornography laws and are therefore illegal. Victims have several legal options available, including filing police reports so prosecutors can attempt to shut down the website, launching lawsuits, filing complaints with data protection authorities, or contacting hosting companies.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
